request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an "Export claims (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) that downloads the claims as a CSV, and the acceptance tests pass: all 4 passed on the second `bin/e2e` run. On the first run, 3 passed but the main "export claims" test failed at its very first step (setting a rate), well before it gets to the export. It passed on the re-run. I think it was a timeout while the app was still starting up, but I didn't confirm that.

**What the file contains:**
- The header `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then one line per claim.
- People appear in list order, including retired people whether they're shown or not. Each person's claims run oldest first, which is the reverse of the on-screen list.
- Each value is worked out the same way the claim row on screen does it, so an empty number or period stays empty and `n/a` stays `n/a`.
- Quoting and line feeds are the same as the people export, because both now use the same code.

This was a front-end-only change; the server and stored data are untouched.

**Files:**
- `src/main/frontend/features/export/exportClaims.slot.tsx` (new): the button and the claims CSV.
- `src/main/frontend/features/export/csv.ts` (new): the quoting and download code, moved out of the people export so both exports use it.
- `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`: the people export now uses `csv.ts`; its output is unchanged.
